item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy-starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings Verstappen in control despite lead changes "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. item.title: Verstappen's superb racecraft & Russell's costly mistake - driver ratings
item.description: Max Verstappen said George Russell's lock-up was "karma" for his comments about the Dutchman earlier in the Las Vegas weekend [Getty Images] Max Verstappen sealed his fourth win of the season with a stunning victory at a chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Red Bull driver fought off his rivals for the lead throughout the race and crossed the line ahead of the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. George Russell, who started second, locked up late on attempting a move on Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and finished ninth, while Charles Leclerc was given a 10-second time penalty for making contact with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton. Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Vegas. Max Verstappen - 10/10 An extraordinary display of racecraft. Inherited pole after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty and spent virtually the entire race being attacked, passed and then finding a way back through, while also working out the optimum energy deployment from inside his Red Bull. One of his finest victories. Lando Norris - 9/10 A remarkable recovery after dropping as low as 11th in the madness of the opening part of the race. Had genuine pace throughout and fought all the way back to second, finishing less than a second behind Verstappen. Oscar Piastri - 9.5/10 One of the drives of the race. Qualified seventh but started 17th because of his engine penalty and charged all the way through to the podium, gaining 14 places and joining McLaren team-mate Norris in passing Antonelli right at the end. Kimi Antonelli - 9.5/10 Fastest of everyone in qualifying and a genuine contender for victory despite starting sixth because of his engine penalty. Battled Verstappen superbly before his Mercedes' energy deployment problem on the final lap cost him two places, although he still recovered fourth from Pierre Gasly before the flag. Pierre Gasly - 9/10 An excellent weekend and comfortably Alpine's best result of the season. Reached Q3, stayed with the leading group throughout and was less than three seconds away from victory at the finish. Franco Colapinto - 8.5/10 Another huge result for Alpine. Qualified inside the top 10, stayed out of trouble while plenty around him didn't and converted ninth on the grid into sixth place. item.title: Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable'
item.description: The Ferrari drivers have previously compromised their own races while battling in Italy and Mexico this season [Getty Images] Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go, costing both points in a race where at one stage they were racing with the McLarens, which finished on the podium. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, which meant he finished 10th, three places behind Hamilton, in a race won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen. It was the second race-compromising incident within grands prix, and it came after the drivers had been brought together to clear the air at the last race in Brazil after their first-lap fighting in Mexico cost them a win. Hamilton said such an incident "should never happen" but added that: "The question should be for Ferrari now." Leclerc said: "We just need to fix whatever is not working." Team principal Frederic Vasseur described the situation as "completely unacceptable". Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide The Frenchman said: "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, the same speech as after Mexico. "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you're passed by others. It means you have to do your race and Charles clearly made a mistake. "It's penalising the team a lot and it's completely unacceptable. Honestly we are more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico, we had a chat together in Brazil, today we passed the message to think about the team when racing together and the outcome is this one." The battle between the two drivers has been tense all season, and in the second part of the year there have been a series of flashpoints, whether it be on-track racing, disputes about how best to work through strategy, and Hamilton ignoring two separate calls to pit in different races, both of which compromised his result, because he was looking at beating Leclerc. Hamilton said: "It's not something I want to really get into." The seven-time champion, who struggled against Leclerc last year but who has been revived in 2026, deflected questions about whether he should be given number-one status. "I've never asked to be number one," he said. "I genuinely haven't ever asked. "There was a point in the season where I was 40-odd points ahead, and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi (Antonelli). "I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year. "At that point, we needed backing to make sure we beat Kimi. There were a few instances in the season where, with the support, I think we could have beaten Kimi. "But no, that's not what I've asked for. We shouldn't have gotten together. item.title: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe
item.description: Real Madrid summer signing is the most clutch substitute in Europe “Juni Calafat and Jose Angel Sanchez gave me a list of 4-5 strikers to choose from in the summer. I chose Carlos Espi.” These were the words of Jose Mourinho after Real Madrid’s win over Celta Vigo last night, a game in which Carlos Espi came off the bench to score the winner, and not for the first time. The manager heavily praised the new signing for his impact, and understandably so given how he has always found a way to come up clutch for Real Madrid, with his numbers being phenomenal. The best in the world As reported by AS , Espi is the most potent goalscoring substitute in all of Europe, and his efficiency in front of goal is second to none, especially under pressure. Espi’s goals have all led to direct points. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) In just about 73 minutes of football for Real Madrid, he has already scored four goals, all of which came in clutch moments. He averages one goal every 18 minutes. What makes the statistics all the more appalling is that he has scored his four goals from just six shots on target and nine overall shots. His goals have directly helped Real Madrid secure six points in La Liga and two in the UEFA Champions League. Thriving under pressure Espi arrived at Real Madrid knowing full well that Kylian Mbappe would be ahead of him on the pecking order. His role was always going to be one of a substitute, and he has embraced that role with minimal fuss. Espi is thriving under pressure. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Yet, the youngster is seemingly enjoying the responsibility of going out and making a difference in chaotic moments, especially with the clock ticking down. Having the manager’s trust as a player who can make a difference under pressure, after all, is something that can make a player supremely confident. Despite not having regular starts, Espi is thus impressing and making the most of his limited minutes at a range that not many saw coming. It remains to be seen if the manager finds any occasional starting role for Espi, especially given how he blatantly refused the possibility of fielding Mbappe and Espi together. What is for sure, however, is that Real Madrid have a pearl on their hands – one that they would likely not trade for any sum of money.

item.title: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top
item.description: Late goals, narrow wins – and back on top The win in the Lower Rhine region was no footballing masterclass, but it was further proof of the resilience of Niko Kovac’s team. Gladbach put BVB under pressure with aggressive pressing, particularly in the first half. The Black & Yellows made technical errors, misplaced passes and found few ways to stretch the opposition defence. Although Felix Nmecha had a chance to put them ahead after just five minutes, BVB generally lacked pace and precision. “We weren’t sharp enough in the first half,” admitted the eventual goalscorer. Sporting director Ole Book also noted unnecessary losses of possession that could not be attributed solely to the hosts’ aggressive approach. With patience and, once again, the right substitutions The picture changed after the break. Borussia Dortmund increased the tempo, took more risks and pushed Gladbach increasingly deep into their own half. Once again, Niko Kovac showed a deft touch with his substitutions. Joey Veerman, Mathis Albert and Marcel Sabitzer were all involved in the build-up to the decisive goal. Albert played in Sabitzer, who laid the ball off for Nmecha. The Germany international unleashed a powerful shot from 19 metres to make it 1-0. It was Nmecha’s fifth goal of the season, already a personal best. The timing is also notable: the midfielder has scored three of his five goals in the final 15 minutes. BVB clearly have the patience and the physical reserves to make a decisive impact even in the closing stages. “We’ve scored late goals a lot now because we have the energy to keep playing our game right to the end,” explained goalkeeper Gregor Kobel. In fact, eight of the Black & Yellows’ 17 Bundesliga goals so far have come in the final ten minutes of matches. Almost half their goals have therefore come at a point when other teams are often already running out of energy and concentration. The fact that BVB left it late in Gladbach did not, however, mean the victory was undeserved. After a laboured first half, the Black & Yellows created considerably more chances. They finished with 2.5 expected goals to Gladbach’s 0.7. “Not spectacular, but deserved — in the manner of a top team,” was Book’s apt assessment. item.title: Victor Wembanyama admits his 50-point game was to ‘show off’ for Selena Gomez
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama subtly dedicated one moment from his 50-point explosion to Selena Gomez. As expected, Wembanyama did that for none other than Gomez, as the Spurs superstar made the admission during the postgame press conference. “Of course I had to show off for Selena, you know,” Wembanyama said while smiling. item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has heaped praise on teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett following his match-winning full debut. The 18-year-old inspired Spurs to a 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town on Saturday, scoring the opener before providing a sublime assist for Dominic Solanke. Academy graduate seizes his Premier League chance Calls for the England Under-19 international to feature had grown louder during a testing 12 months at Spurs, over a year after his senior bow at 16. Following two bright substitute cameos, De Zerbi finalised plans 10 days before Saturday's clash against Ipswich to hand him a maiden top-flight start. Williams-Barnett struck the opener on 15 minutes before embarking on a mazy second-half run to set up Solanke. De Zerbi outlines Maddison plan and defensive demands De Zerbi explained that pairing the teenager closely with James Maddison was key to his freedom, alongside strict instructions issued on Thursday regarding his defensive work rate. "Luca is a special player," De Zerbi said. "I'm not surprised, because his talent is bigger than you think. He played very well. I think he's lucky, because he's playing in a top club, with top teammates. "I decided to play today with Luca from 10 days and in my plan, it was Maddison and Luca very close to speak the same language, to play together and the experience of Maddison I thought could be important. The behaviour of Maddison could help him to play with freedom. "And Thursday, I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things. Just two things. To play like he plays on the park with his friends, with the same freedom. "And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembele, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal, because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are the attackers. Even if they are Ballon d'Or winners, or any way the players with talent, they have to work on the pitch." YouTube inspiration fuels Yamal comparisons De Zerbi backed the 18-year-old to eventually match Barcelona prodigy Yamal, pointing to his relaxed preparation on the team bus as evidence of his rare mentality. "Yes, I think so," when asked whether Williams-Barnett can reach Yamal's level. "And one of the best things in my career... item.description: Lewis Hamilton insists Ferrari needs to “sort out” how their drivers go racing after the Briton and Charles Leclerc collided once again at the Las Vegas Grand Prix . Three weeks on from their high-profile incident in Mexico City , which prompted a furious reaction from Hamilton, the Ferrari drivers clashed again on Saturday night in Sin City as they tussled for a handful of points. While fighting in the bottom half of the top-10, Leclerc surged down the inside at turn seven and Hamilton clipped his wheel, spinning the British driver. Hamilton in the end finished seventh, while Leclerc finished 10th after receiving a 10-second penalty from the stewards for the incident. Hamilton, who has implored his Ferrari outfit to clarify their policy when it comes to team orders, was level-headed after the race but acknowledged that the Scuderia need to clarify racing rules between the two drivers. “I’m not going to get into the scenario - that’s something to speak to Ferrari about,” he told Sky Sports F1 after the race, which was won by Red Bull ’s Max Verstappen . “We knew we were faced with another challenge today. item.title: Expected Goals stats tell the very real story after Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2
item.description: Harvey Barnes Shooting Goal Newcastle v Arsenal Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game. To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing. Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match. With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value. The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot. The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match. So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc. These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48 As you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one. When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall. As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical. item.title: Noni Madueke: That wasn’t good enough
item.description: Noni Madueke: That wasn’t good enough Despite scoring the goal that rescued a point, Noni Madueke was left frustrated by the way Arsenal allowed control of the game to slip at Newcastle. Photo by George Wood/Getty Images Noni Madueke has admitted Arsenal ’s start to the second half against Newcastle United “wasn’t good enough” after the visitors had to come from behind to earn a 2-2 draw at St James’ Park despite dominating the first half. Madueke scored Arsenal’s equaliser in the 78th minute, but his reaction afterwards told of the frustration within in the Arsenal camp after they let the game get away from them. Arsenal had been the significantly better side before the break and went ahead through Eberechi Eze in the 33rd minute. Madueke felt they had created enough opportunities to put themselves in a stronger position and included himself among those who should have done better. “I think we’re a little bit disappointed that we didn’t come away with three points, especially with how well we played in the first half,” Madueke said . Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images “We had opportunities to win the game, myself included, but that’s football. “I think the way we came out in the second half wasn’t good enough from our part, but we showed character to get a point in the end. “We take it, we move on, we watch the film back, and see where we can improve.” In what was a classic ‘game of two halves’, Harvey Barnes equalised four minutes into the second half before Malick Thiaw put Newcastle ahead in the 62nd minute after Arsenal had suffocated the Magpies in the first half. Madueke’s goal 16 minutes later prevented Arsenal leaving empty-handed, but he did not allow the equaliser to disguise the frustration at their second half performance. Speaking to BBC Match of the Day , he said , “A draw at St James’ Park is not the end of the world but it’s disappointing. “I think we let it slip. They came out with more intensity and fight but I feel it was on us. The principles and concepts we played with in the first half weren’t there at the start of the second.” Photo by George Wood/Getty Images His assessment to Sky Sports followed the same line. Madueke said Arsenal had been “outstanding” before half-time, only for their level to drop during the opening 20 minutes of the second half. He questioned whether they had become “too relaxed” after the quality of their first-half display, although he ultimately said 2-2 was a fair result. Madueke also had chances before the break which he felt he should have taken, so scoring the equaliser did not leave him entirely satisfied with his own evening. “I missed a couple of chances in the first half so that kind of brought me back to neutral,” he said. item.title: Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Maresca admits Man City must tighten up defensively amid winless run») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City must tighten up defensively after their winless run continued with a frustrating 1-1 draw against Fulham. City needed an equalizer from Elliot Anderson at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday to avoid a fourth successive Premier League defeat. Anderson’s volley just before the hour mark cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener and, although City were aggrieved that Erling Haaland had a goal disallowed, there was no disguising another disappointing display. City manager Maresca said: “For sure we are conceding too many goals. We need to avoid that. “Sometimes you need to win games 1-0, you need to keep clean sheets and unfortunately, at this moment, we are not able to do that. This is the main thing. “I think we concede almost 80%of our goals in the first 20 minutes, so for sure there is something there that we need to improve. “But I can see many positive aspects and this is something we started four months ago, not four years ago.” The main talking point of the game was referee Thomas Bramall’s decision to chalk off what would have been a leveller from Haaland in the 25th minute. The Norwegian bundled home from close range after Bernd Leno had failed to gather a shot cleanly, but the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. Haaland was perplexed, but the decision was upheld by VAR and the striker then uncharacteristically spurned another good chance soon after. It was left to Anderson to salvage a point for City from what was a largely lacklustre performance. The midfielder marked his return to action after being sent off for England last week when he struck with a low volley from the edge of the area after a corner was cleared. Anderson told the club’s website: “It was a poor first half, unfortunately. We seem to have been going behind recently, but the reaction was really good after half-time. “It just wasn’t enough to get the three points. We had plenty of chances, which seems to be the overall story [lately], but once they start going in, and as maybe we start picking our performances up a little bit more, we’ll be happy.” With Enzo Fernandez on the bench after returning later from international duty, Anderson was deployed in a more advanced role by Maresca. “I played a little bit higher up and got myself a goal,” Anderson said. “I’m just trying to just work on my game. “We tweaked a few things and really went for them, which gave us a bit more control of the game. It’s just unlucky we didn’t get the second.”

item.title: Max Verstappen labels George Russell a ‘joke’ and ‘so far below my level’ in stinging remarks
item.description: Max Verstappen declared that George Russell was “so far below my level” in a series of stinging remarks about his Formula 1 rival after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix . The duo, who clashed in a series of heated confrontations on track and in the media at the end of the 2024 season, have reignited their rivalry this weekend in Las Vegas after an incident in final practice on Saturday. Russell stated that Verstappen “screwed him over” after the pair collided, adding that the Dutchman believes he is “bigger and better than everyone else.” The pair started on the front row and astonishingly traded places with Russell 12 times during a breathless race in Sin City. Yet with a handful of laps remaining, Russell misjudged an overtake on teammate Kimi Antonelli and hit the barrier. Verstappen stormed to victory while the Briton finished down in ninth. "Ha ha, well done! My God," laughed Verstappen on team radio when the incident occurred. Then, in an interview with Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay, Verstappen took aim at Russell. "This actually had nothing to do with Formula 1," he said "But I did enjoy some of the action. Especially because one person in particular didn't stand a chance. He [Russell] deserves that too. “His comments don't motivate me, because he's nowhere near me. All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect Karma." Speaking later in the FIA press conference, Verstappen elaborated: "It doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. "So it doesn't bother me. And today, Karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. "I was like, 'Fantastic, my day is only getting better.' And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete." Verstappen and Russell also clashed last year after the Dutchman deliberately rammed the Mercedes driver at the Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona. In a season where the majority had Russell as the pre-season favourite, his Mercedes teammate Antonelli has romped to the world championship while second-placed Verstappen is now 40 points clear of Russell with two rounds remaining. The next round is the Qatar Grand Prix on 29 November.

item.description: Barcelona face fresh hurdle in pursuit of key target as his club demand more than €20m – report According to SPORT , Barcelona have stepped up their efforts to sign Ruud Nijstad from FC Twente ahead of the January transfer window, but the Dutch club are making an agreement difficult. The 18-year-old centre-back has become one of the Catalan giants’ preferred defensive targets , but any move for the youngster will be complicated due to Twente’s demands. Nijstad open to Barcelona move Having already tried to sign Nijstad in the summer, Barcelona have renewed contact with Twente in an attempt to revive the operation in the January transfer window. Nijstad was initially inclined to continue his development in the Netherlands, but his position has softened after learning more about the sporting project being offered by the La Liga champions. The 18-year-old starlet is particularly attracted by Barcelona’s willingness to give opportunities to emerging players. As such, he sees the Blaugrana as the ideal environment to continue his development, making a move to Camp Nou increasingly appealing. Barcelona want Nijstad in January. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB) While this is an encouraging development as far as Barcelona are concerned, convincing the player is only part of the challenge. Twente demand more than €20 million Indeed, as per the report, Twente’s financial demands are making the transfer increasingly complicated. The Dutch club have raised their asking price and are now demanding more than €20 million to sanction his departure. A left-footed centre-back with an impressive ability to play out from the back, Barça see the teenager as a good fit into their tactical setup. However, Barcelona consider that figure excessive for an 18-year-old who still has relatively limited experience at the highest level. Although the Catalans are convinced by Nijstad’s potential, they are reluctant to commit such a substantial amount to a player whose development is far from complete. Barcelona do not want to spend big on Nijstad. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Moreover, Twente want to retain Nijstad until the end of the current campaign, even if they agree to sell him during the January window. The Dutch club would consider negotiating a permanent transfer in January on the condition that the teenage defender returns to them on loan until June. For Barcelona, however, the idea does not fit with their intention to bring Nijstad in during the winter window, making the possibility of a deal extremely difficult. Beyond these two complications, Barcelona also have to deal with the fact hat the youngster is attracting interest from the Premier League. Chelsea, Manchester City and Manchester United are all monitoring Nijstad’s development, and their interest could make an already difficult negotiation even more complex.

KEY TAKEAWAYS: Robin Uthappa has been appointed Mumbai Indians ' batting coach ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He says the five-time champions feel like underdogs and must earn back supporters' trust. Mumbai finished ninth in 2026 and have gone six seasons without a title. Robin Uthappa says Mumbai Indians feel like underdogs going into IPL 2027 Five titles usually buy a franchise some patience, but Mumbai Indians have not won one since 2020 and finished ninth last season with four wins from 14 matches. Their new batting coach is not pretending otherwise. Robin Uthappa, who took the job as part of a wholesale change to the coaching staff, framed the coming season in terms most people associate with a struggling side rather than the most decorated in the competition. "As Mumbai Indians, we feel like we're underdogs," he said in an interaction with select media, reported by NDTV . He went further on what the squad owes the people who follow it. "We really need to earn our stripes back and earn the trust of the fans. There are a lot of things that we have to work towards as a team," Uthappa added. The appointment itself caught him off guard. "It completely came from left field. I didn't see it coming," said the two-time IPL winner, who is currently commentating at the DP World ILT20 in the UAE, adding that he had been hoping for a call from the franchise because he believed he could add value to it. What Mumbai Indians have changed after six seasons without an IPL title Uthappa is one piece of an overhaul that has touched almost every part of the setup. Kieron Pollard, who held the batting role last season, has been elevated to head coach, former India fielding coach T Dilip takes the fielding brief, and Mitchell McClenaghan returns to the franchise as bowling coach. The playing side has moved just as far. Hardik Pandya, who captained through the ninth-place finish, has gone to Punjab Kings in the trade that brought Arshdeep Singh the other way, and Mumbai have changed captain for 2027, with Rohit Sharma widely reported to be taking the job back. Uthappa's answer to all of it was to talk about humility rather than personnel. "Nobody is bigger than Mother Cricket. We've all been in the game long enough to know that nobody can beat Mother Cricket. You have to operate from that humility," he said. He described his own role as a supporting one rather than a corrective one. "I'm only a mirror to them, holding them accountable for what they want to achieve and aligning that with the larger goal of the team," Uthappa said. item.description: Nearly two full months into the season, the Chicago Blackhawks finally earned their first road win in 10 tries on Saturday night, defeating the Calgary Flames 4-3 in overtime at Scotiabank Saddledome. The Blackhawks were the only NHL team still without a road win entering Saturday, and they had to overcome plenty of adversity to change that in Calgary. The countless hardships and seemingly never-ending misfortune in the first quarter of this season are starting to harden the young Hawks group. Already without captain Connor Bedard in the lineup for the second straight game due to his latest shoulder injury , the Blackhawks also lost defenseman Wyatt Kaiser and center Anton Frondell on Saturday, leaving only 16 skaters for the third period and overtime. With a shortened visiting bench, and the Flames carrying all the momentum late after clawing back from a 3-1 deficit, the Blackhawks dug deep to push the game to 3-on-3 play. Then, after Frank Nazar drew a penalty with a tremendous solo effort, the power play converted just after Yegor Sharangovich stepped out of the penalty box, with Sam Rinzel fittingly responsible for the game-winner. “I thought our guys, with the loss of Frondell and Kaiser, we had to gut it out. Especially after giving up the early goal in the third [period]. It wasn’t necessarily our best third, but we found a way to bend not break.” Another obstacle the Hawks faced was an overturned overtime-winner from Roman Kantserov , who became the first NHL rookie to reach 10 goals this season earlier in the game. Kantserov’s net-front tap-in from Patrick Kane ‘s pass was reversed for a careless offside by Nazar, setting the stage for another potential disastrous loss that would have perfectly described the tumultuous season thus far. But despite all the bumps in the road, the Blackhawks stuck with it and found a second game-winning goal in overtime, with no dispute from the Flames or video review necessary for Rinzel’s tally. Since the disastrous three-game Southeastern road trip and GM Kyle Davidson’s state-of-the-union press conference, the Blackhawks have done well to smooth the waters around a rocking ship. They’re now 3-1-1 in the last five games, and all three wins have been character-builders. Their win over the Buffalo Sabres on Nov. 12 marked the first time they earned two points when trailing entering the third period this season. That victory was particularly needed, considering it was the Hawks’ first game after an embarrassing 9-2 loss in Carolina. Then, when Bedard got injured in Tuesday’s game against the Toronto Maple Leafs, the Blackhawks didn’t let it take the wind out of their sails and sealed the win for their captain, scoring a season-high six goals. Now, the Blackhawks have won away from the United Center for the first time this year, which should give the group added confidence that they can do it again on Sunday in Vancouver. item.title: 'Right now Malen is extraordinary!' - Gian Piero Gasperini explains how former Aston Villa striker matched a 66-year Roma record with four-goal Parma demolition
item.description: FBL-ITA-SERIE A-PARMA-ROMA - AFP Donyell Malen netted four goals in Roma's 5-1 Serie A demolition of Parma to equal an all-time club record for calendar-year league strikes. Coach Gian Piero Gasperini hailed the former Aston Villa forward as "extraordinary" after his 26th Serie A goal of 2026 kept the Giallorossi within two points of leaders Lazio. Malen hits four to equal 66-year Roma record Donyell Malen scored four times to inspire Roma to an emphatic 5-1 Serie A victory over Parma and keep Gian Piero Gasperini's side just two points behind league leaders Lazio. Rodrigo Mora added Roma's other goal after Nesta Elphege had briefly equalised on the counter-attack for the hosts. The four-goal haul took Malen to 12 goals in the opening 12 league rounds and 26 Serie A strikes across the 2026 calendar year since arriving from Aston Villa in January. That tally draws the Netherlands international level with Pedro Manfredini's all-time club record set in 1960, with more than a month of the year still remaining. Gasperini explains why Malen thrives in his system Speaking to DAZN Italia after the final whistle, Gasperini praised his team's response to conceding an equaliser and singled out Malen's tactical compatibility with Roma's attacking style. "Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, you don't play at that level without quality," Gasperini said. "Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way. There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents, and of course Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary. He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn't fit as well with our style of football." From Villa loanee to record-breaking talisman Malen initially joined Roma on loan from Aston Villa on 16 January 2026 before completing a permanent €25 million move in May on a contract running until June 2030 after firing the club back into the UEFA Champions League. His latest four-goal outing also marked his third Serie A hat-trick of 2026—a feat last achieved in the Italian top flight by Josip Ilicic, who also played under Gasperini at Atalanta. Roma's 36 goals across their first 12 league fixtures represent the highest total by any Serie A team in 76 years, since Inter, Milan and Juventus all surpassed that mark in the 1950-51 season. Title race momentum builds with fixtures left in 2026 With Roma sitting on 30 points and chasing Lazio at the summit, Gasperini noted that overcoming adversity at Parma showed his squad's growing belief. item.description: BLOOMINGTON — Todd Yeagley isn’t shy about breaking one of coaching’s oldest and most trusted codes when he thinks the time is right. item.title: Boise State CFP Picture Changes With Loss; Liberty, New Mexico, UTSA Notice
item.description: FORT COLLINS, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 7: Head coach Spencer Danielson of the Boise State Broncos celebrates after a touchdown in the first quarter of the game against the Colorado State Rams at Canvas Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Fort Collins, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) Getty Most college football fans were asleep when the game-winning field goal went through. But at about 1:10 a.m. ET, San Diego State drilled a 3-pointer at the buzzer to stun Boise State, 22-20. With that make came a potentially drastic shakeup to the College Football Playoff picture for Group of 6 teams. One Group of 6 team gets into this year’s 12-team field automatically, and it was shaping up to be the Broncos. All of a sudden, that’s not so certain. Fans of Liberty, New Mexico and UTSA are all watching closely. Boise State CFP Picture The reality is that Boise State, even with the loss, may remain in the driver’s seat for that spot, but with a lot less margin for error. The Broncos were ranked No. 17 this week by the CFP committee, and no other Group of 6 team was ranked in the top-25 at all. That would suggest the committee viewed the gap as pretty wide. Before this, Boise State’s only loss was to Oregon. Boise State will be watching closely to see where it slots this week. The Broncos have just one game left, the Pac-12 title game. If Boise State had won out, there would’ve been no question here. But with the surprise loss, the door has been opened up to the rest of the Group of 6. Group of 6 Playoff Picture: Liberty, New Mexico, UTSA If New Mexico hadn’t recently been upset by UNLV, the Lobos might have a chance to leapfrog Boise State right now. As is, these teams will all get a bit closer together. Liberty looks the best in a quick look on paper. They’re 10-1 with a 7-0 conference record and still a conference title game to play, but the Flames have also played a brutally poor schedule. That won’t do them any favors. New Mexico is still in the picture after a key win over Wyoming on Friday night. The American Conference leader, UTSA (Texas-San Antonio), is now 9-2 after Saturday and still alive here, too. These other Group of 6 teams would likely have their best chance if Boise State loses in their conference championship game in a couple of weeks. All these other contenders can do is close with wins and then hope. We’ll get a great hint on Tuesday night, though, when the CFP committee releases another rankings. Will Boise State still be in the top-25? Will a different Group of 6 team be there? There’s a lot still to be decided, and San Diego State’s stunning upset certainly left this door quite a bit more open. item.title: Wembanyama hits 50 points in dominant Spurs win
item.description: Victor Wembanyama was selected by the San Antonio Spurs with the first overall pick in the 2023 NBA draft. [Reuters] San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama hit 50 points in a historic performance as his side beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91. The 22-year-old, who is 7ft 4ins tall, became the first player with 50 points, five blocks and five three-pointers in a match since the NBA added threes in 1979–80. The France international, who was defensive player of the year for 2026, said he put on a show for a celebrity-packed crowd which included actress and long-time Spurs fan Selena Gomez. "I had to show off for Selena," he said. "I just want to keep stacking them [records] up. I don't plan on doing those. They just come and we play the right way as a team. "So, I just want to stack them up. Hopefully there's many more coming." The Spurs have made a fine start to the season, winning 14 of their 17 games so far to top the Western Conference Southwest. They won the division last season before losing to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson added. "It's a cliche to say, 'Why doesn't he do it every game?' "But it's so interesting when people play like that, especially with his talent." 'I'm not very good at stat-padding' Wembanyama's haul - the third of his career - came after James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games on Saturday. Wilt Chamberlain holds the record with an incredible 118 50-point games. "It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat-padding," Wembanyama said. "So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have." Wembanyama was later asked whether there was an ethical right or wrong way to score 50 points. Some NBA players have been accused of chasing individual statistics for financial gain instead of concentrating on their team's results. "Maybe, I think that's a question for you. The greats, they don't think about that," Wembanyama replied. "I don't think LeBron [James], Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander], [Nikola] Jokic, [Luka] Doncic, I don't think they think about that. I have them as examples, so I'm trying to not think about it either."

item.description: FBL-MLS-INTER MIAMI-COLUMBUS CREW - AFP The dream of a back-to-back MLS Cup glory for Lionel Messi and Inter Miami is hanging by a thread following a disastrous 3-0 home defeat to the Columbus Crew. Despite entering the postseason as heavy favorites, the defending champions were dismantled in their first-ever playoff appearance at Nu Stadium on Saturday night. Self-inflicted errors spark Miami collapse Inter Miami fell behind after eight minutes when goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair rushed off his line and fouled Gonzalo Tapia in the box, allowing the forward to convert from the spot. Messi was then denied by a spectacular save from USMNT goalkeeper Patrick Schulte, while Luis Suarez poked wide with the goal at his mercy. St. Clair made smart stops to keep the deficit at 1-0, but defender Gonzalo Lujan collected two yellow cards for a 36th-minute red card before a frustrated Messi was booked for throwing the ball straight into Tapia's face from close range. Columbus punished the 10-man hosts with two goals in six early second-half minutes as Taha Habroune side-footed in Brais Méndez's through ball and Tapia turned Yannick Bright to race clear, allowing Crew interim coach Laurent Courtois to withdraw the striker with over 30 minutes left to preserve his legs and avoid a second booking. Gonzalez rues missed chances and turning point Inter Miami boss Kily Gonzalez blamed early missed opportunities and Lujan's dismissal for the defeat. "The team created four or five clear-cut chances to put the game away, but we couldn't convert, and their goalkeeper made the saves," Gonzalez told reporters. "Then came the red card, which completely changed the nature of the match. "But focusing on the 11 vs 11, we created plenty of chances; it was just one of those games where nothing goes your way, you just have to bite your tongue and endure it. There's still another leg to play - we have to go there, win and then come back and define it at home. I take full responsibility." Contrasting form exposes Miami's slump Second-seeded Miami, featuring Golden Boot winner and MVP favourite Messi, finished 13 points above seventh-seeded Columbus, yet have just five wins in their past 18 MLS matches and six in 17 at their new 26,700-seat Nu Stadium since April, failing to score there for the first time. item.title: 'Leave him alone' - Como boss Cesc Fabregas calls for Argentina to retire Lionel Messi's number 10 shirt to protect Nico Paz
item.description: Argentina v Costa Rica - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Como head coach Cesc Fabregas has urged the Argentina national team to retire Lionel Messi’s iconic number 10 jersey to shield Nico Paz from unfair expectations. The Spanish tactician believes that the young playmaker needs space to develop without the crushing weight of following in the footsteps of arguably the greatest player in history. Protecting the next generation The rise of Paz has sparked a significant debate regarding the future of the famous number 10 shirt for the Albiceleste . Following Messi's eventual departure from the international stage, many have pointed to the Como starlet as a natural successor . However, Fabregas has taken a firm stance against the idea, suggesting that the shirt should be permanently shelved out of respect for Messi and to protect the mental well-being of his young charge. He believes that placing such a historic burden on a developing player could be detrimental to their long-term growth. Fabregas is keen to ensure that the spotlight remains manageable for the 20-year-old, who has impressed in Serie A since his move from Real Madrid. The manager's comments underline a desire to avoid the "new Messi" tags that have hindered many young talents in the past. "Leave him alone. The number 10 is for Messi and that is it, it must be retired," the former Arsenal and Barcelona midfielder stated emphatically, as cited by TUTTOmercatoWEB . Managing international fatigue Beyond the symbolic weight of the jersey, Fabregas also addressed the physical toll that international duty takes on his squad. He noted that while representing one's country is a vital step for a player's career, it requires careful management upon their return to club football. The Como boss highlighted how Paz struggled physically after his initial call-up to the Argentina squad, appearing fatigued during a subsequent domestic fixture against Parma. "Yes, it helps that they go. Lucas [Da Cunha] is not too young, he is 25, but he has exploded very quickly. At the beginning, you struggle a bit. I remember Nico the first time in the national team, he came back and against Parma he was dead, he was walking on the pitch even though he had scored. You could see he wasn't himself. Now they manage themselves better," Fabregas said. Integration of rising stars The manager also touched upon the progress of Da Cunha and the workload of other squad members like Perrone. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
